## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `omission-cost-asymmetric-ranking`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-07-29T04:53:05.081Z.

Entry slug omission-cost-asymmetric-ranking. Purpose: rank candidates by the expected regret of leaving them out, not by the probability that they are relevant. Every scorer in this catalog optimises a value-per-token quantity in which a candidate's contribution is symmetric - including a marginal item costs tokens, excluding it costs the value it would have carried. That symmetry is false for one important class. A Decision that forbids the approach an agent is about to take has low lexical similarity to the task, low recency, and possibly no edge to the work at hand, so every existing signal ranks it out; and omitting it costs a wrong implementation, a review cycle, and a revert. Mechanism. Attach to each candidate an omission-loss term L_omit(i) that is learned rather than declared, estimated from the record: the fraction of past episodes in which the item was NOT served, and the retrieving agent's subsequent work was later superseded, reverted, reopened, or became the source of a discovered_from edge pointing back at the item. All four of those are already typed edges or recorded status transitions, so the label is derivable from immutable history with no new stored state, exactly as the learning-to-rank entry derives its pairwise labels. Combine as score(i) = base_value(i) + lambda * P(task class matches the item's constraint scope) * L_omit(i), keeping the whole expression linear so explain-ranking stays truthful. Constraint-bearing types - accepted Decisions, open ADRs, items whose acceptance criteria contain a prohibition - form the prior class that starts with a nonzero L_omit before any evidence accumulates, because the cold-start cost of learning this from scratch is paid in exactly the incidents it exists to prevent. Distinction from neighbours. Value-per-token and marginal-utility-per-token price inclusion; this prices exclusion, and the two differ only when the loss is asymmetric, which is the whole point. Outcome-distance-prior asks how close an item is to a goal; this asks what breaks if the agent never sees it. Verify-before-serve gates whether a served fact is trustworthy; this gates whether an untrusted-but-critical fact should be served anyway. Degenerate case that must be proved as a no-op: with L_omit uniform across all candidates the added term is a constant and the ranking is bit-identical to the existing marginal-utility ordering. A workspace with no supersedes, no reopen and no discovered_from edges therefore behaves exactly as today, which also means a brand-new workspace pays nothing.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
